Party On
PAR-tee ON
interjection, phrase (Gen X slang)
American youth slang for "keep enjoying yourself, carry on celebrating," current in the 1980s; made famous as the sign-off of Wayne Campbell and Garth Algar ("Party on, Wayne." "Party on, Garth.") in the SNL "Wayne’s World" sketches (from 1989) and the film Wayne’s World (1992). Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989) closes with the cognate "Be excellent to each other, and party on, dudes!"

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Party on is a blessing in the grammar of the basement: keep going, keep having fun, may the good times never stop. Wayne and Garth used it as a greeting and a farewell, and a generation adopted it as a creed. The Christian observation is that Scripture is not against feasting — the Lord turned water into wine at a wedding, and Nehemiah told a weeping people, "Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet … for the joy of the LORD is your strength" (Neh 8:10). But Scripture refuses to make the party the point. The Preacher tested it: "I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity" (Ecc 2:1). "It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men" (Ecc 7:2). The rich fool said, "Soul … take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry," and God said, "Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee" (Luk 12:19-20). The joy that does not end is found elsewhere: "in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore" (Psa 16:11). Party on, says the basement; feast in the presence of God, says the gospel, at a table that will outlast every party.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X blessing of perpetual fun ("Party on, Wayne," SNL 1989; film 1992); Scripture allows the feast but refuses to make it the point — fulness of joy is in God’s presence (Psa 16:11).

expand to see more

PARTY ON, interj. (Gen X slang, 1980s; popularized 1989–92) Keep having a good time; carry on enjoying yourself. Used as greeting, farewell, or toast.

Signature line of Wayne and Garth ("Party on, Wayne." "Party on, Garth."); cf. Bill & Ted: "Be excellent to each other, and party on, dudes!"

Kin to party animal and excellent!; the creed of the suburban basement.

Webster 1828: PARTY, n. [Latin pars. See Part.] 1. A number of persons united in opinion or design, in opposition to others in the community. …

Decode for parents: Scripture blesses the feast and forbids making it the meaning of life (Ecc 2:1; Luk 12:19-20).

Key Scripture

Ecc 2:1 — "I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also is vanity."

Ecc 7:2 — "It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart."

Luk 12:19 — "And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry."

Neh 8:10 — "Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength."

Psa 16:11 — "Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore."

Modern Corruption

Party on makes perpetual fun the blessing of life; Scripture allows the feast, tests mirth and finds it vanity, and places the joy that never ends in the presence of God.

expand to see more

Fun as the highest good. The basement creed is a soft hedonism: no great evil intended, only the assumption that the purpose of life is to keep the good times rolling. The Preacher ran that experiment with more money than any teenager and reported back: "this also is vanity" (Ecc 2:1). The rich fool of Luke 12 is the man who never stopped partying on and never prepared for the night his soul was required.

The better feast. The Bible’s alternative is not gloom but a holy feast: Nehemiah’s people eating the fat and drinking the sweet because "this day is holy unto our Lord" (Neh 8:10), and sending portions to the poor. The Christian may feast with a clear conscience when the feast points beyond itself, to the One in whose presence is fulness of joy (Psa 16:11).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin partire (to divide) → French partie → English party (a social gathering) → 1980s party on → "Wayne’s World" (1989–92); Scripture: joy for evermore at God’s right hand (Psa 16:11).

expand to see more

Latin partire — to divide → French partie — a side, a company

English party — a faction; by the 18th c., a social gathering

1980s American youth: to party, party on — keep celebrating

1989–92: Wayne and Garth’s signature; Bill & Ted (1989)

Biblical feasting: holy unto the Lord (Neh 8:10); mirth tested and found vain (Ecc 2:1)

Usage

""Party on, Garth." "Party on, Wayne.""

"The rich fool partied on until the night his soul was required (Luk 12:20)."

"Feast, and send portions to the poor, because the day is holy unto the Lord (Neh 8:10)."
